描述_EN: the shape of the vessel, characterised by a hemispherical bowl on a high stem, was extensively reproduced during the song dynasty (960-1279) when a taste for archaic objects was shared by the imperial court and wealthy élites. the tiny interlaced snake-like creatures, which decorate many eastern zhou bronzes, are used on this example as background to a pattern of small protruding beads distributed symmetrically on the surface. during the western zhou dynasty (1050-771 bc) it became routine to cast these vessels in bronze and use them in various ceremonies and death rituals. this traditional vessel, called a dou in chinese, was produced between 525-475 bc during the eastern zhou period (771-221 bc). vessels of this sort had been produced since the neolithic period (5000-1700 bc), but were typically made of ceramic in many regions of china.
描述_ZN: 此器形状的特点是高柄半球形碗，在宋朝（960-1279）期间被广泛复制，当时朝廷和富有的贵族们都喜欢古物。 小的交错的蛇形生物，装饰了许多东周的青铜器，在这个例子中，作为背景，小的突出的珠子图案对称地分布在表面上。 在西周时期（公元前1050-771年），用青铜铸造这些器皿并将其用于各种仪式和死亡仪式成为惯例。 这种传统的器皿，在中国被称为斗，是在公元前525-475年的东周时期（公元前771-221年）生产的。 这种容器从新石器时代（公元前5000-1700年）就开始生产了，但在中国的许多地区通常是由陶瓷制成的。
